security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, Chinese text entropy, and graph-community iteration. The Python rule engine still uses eval on condition strings and fails open when evaluation raises an exception. The sample backtest also miscalculates capture and false-positive rates, so it should not guide production decisions unchanged.

remediation.issue: The rule engine evaluates condition strings with Python eval.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a parsed expression language and an operator allowlist. Validate field names, value types, and syntax before rule activation.

remediation.issue: Rule evaluation errors silently produce a non-match.
remediation.suggestion: Route evaluation failures to REVIEW or an explicit error. Log invalid rules and prevent their activation until validation succeeds.

remediation.issue: The backtest sample calculates capture and false-positive rates with incorrect populations.
remediation.suggestion: Calculate detected fraud over all fraud and rejected legitimate cases over all legitimate cases. Add tests with known confusion matrices.

semantic_findings.title: Rule Evaluation Fails Open
semantic_findings.description: Any exception while checking a fraud rule returns false, so malformed conditions silently bypass that control instead of stopping or escalating the decision.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception handler directly returns false for every evaluation error. In this engine, false means the rule does not trigger.

semantic_findings.title: Backtest Metrics Misstate Control Effectiveness
semantic_findings.description: Capture rate is calculated as fraud prevalence, while false-positive rate uses all labeled rows as the denominator. Both can mislead deployment decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The formulas do not condition capture rate on detected fraud or false-positive rate on legitimate cases. The code is explicit.

content.value_statement: Fraud teams need structured controls that balance loss prevention with customer impact. This skill provides practical templates for analysis, rules, models, backtesting, and architecture.
actual_capabilities: Identifies fraud scenarios, attack paths, affected processes, and control gaps from a business description.
Drafts prioritized rule catalogs with conditions, decisions, scope, and backtesting guidance.
Provides feature engineering templates for device, IP, transaction, and behavior sequence data.
Outlines XGBoost training and evaluation for imbalanced fraud classification.
Provides anomaly detection and graph-community templates for suspicious group discovery.
Designs real-time risk architectures using streaming, feature storage, decision engines, monitoring, and model inference.
limitations: All templates require adaptation, validation, and testing with representative business data.
The sample rule evaluator uses Python eval and is unsafe for untrusted conditions.
The sample backtest calculations require correction before operational use.
The skill does not provide live threat intelligence, production deployment, or regulatory approval.

use_cases.title: Plan Controls for a New Journey
use_cases.description: Map abuse paths and draft layered controls for registration, promotions, payments, withdrawals, or content publishing.

use_cases.title: Build and Evaluate Risk Features
use_cases.description: Define behavioral features, select model metrics, and prepare a time-aware validation approach for labeled events.

use_cases.title: Design a Real-Time Decision Platform
use_cases.description: Plan streaming data, online features, rule evaluation, model inference, decision routing, monitoring, and storage.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Fraud Scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze fraud risks for [business journey]. Identify abuse types, attack steps, affected assets, warning signals, and existing control gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a clear business journey and known constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Design Layered Risk Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create controls for [risk scenario] using rules, models, lists, and manual review. Define priorities, decisions, conflicts, and required data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after the main abuse paths are understood.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Strategy Backtest
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a time-based backtest for [strategy] using this schema: [fields]. Define labels, metrics, thresholds, segments, costs, and leakage checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before activating a new rule or model.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Production Risk System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a risk platform for [business] at [QPS] with [latency target]. Cover ingestion, features, decisions, resilience, observability, privacy, and rollout.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a new platform or a major system upgrade.

output_examples.input: Assess account takeover risk during password reset.
output_examples.output: Primary risks include credential stuffing, recovery-channel takeover, and session theft. Recommended controls combine device history, velocity limits, step-up verification, and review routing.

output_examples.input: Plan a backtest for a high-frequency payment rule.
output_examples.output: Use a time-based holdout, transaction-level labels, and customer segments. Report fraud capture, legitimate rejection, review volume, prevented loss, and confidence intervals.

output_examples.input: Design a real-time fraud platform for 5,000 requests per second.
output_examples.output: Use streaming ingestion, online and offline feature stores, versioned rules, model serving, deterministic decision routing, replay support, and metric-driven gradual rollout.

best_practices: Validate every control on a time-based holdout and report customer impact by segment.
Use versioned rules, monitored features, staged rollout, and rapid rollback.
Combine deterministic rules with models and manual review for uncertain cases.
anti_patterns: Do not execute untrusted rule text with eval or another general-purpose interpreter.
Do not select thresholds using only aggregate accuracy or fraud prevalence.
Do not deploy controls without ownership, monitoring, appeal paths, and rollback criteria.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to production data?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis and implementation templates based on information supplied in the conversation.

faq.question: Can it produce fraud rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft rule conditions, priorities, decisions, scopes, and backtesting requirements for review.

faq.question: Can it train a production model?
faq.answer: It provides a training template and evaluation guidance. Production training requires validated data, secure infrastructure, monitoring, and independent review.

faq.question: Which fraud domains are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers ecommerce, finance, content platforms, games, registration, promotions, payments, account takeover, and related abuse.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Minimize shared data, remove direct identifiers, enforce access controls, and follow applicable privacy, retention, and audit requirements.

faq.question: Is the included rule engine production ready?
faq.answer: No. Replace dynamic eval, add strict validation, fail safely, test rule conflicts, and implement observability before production use.
